Date of concluding arguments : 13.02.2023  Date of decision : 18.03.2023 AWARD/JUDGMENT 1.

The claim for compensation raised in this claim petition is in respect of fatal injuries alleged to have been sustained by the deceased Sh. Ashok Kumar in a road accident that took place on 12.07.2016, at about 07.05 PM, Near Pillar No. 135, Subroto Park, New Delhi, regarding which one FIR No.245/2016, under Sections 279/304-A IPC & Sections 146/196 MV Act was registered at PS Delhi Cantt.

The vehicle involved in this case is an army truck bearing registration No.
09C088677N, which at the relevant time of accident was being driven by respondent no.1 (R1) and owned by respondent no. 2 (R2).
2.
The claimants are the wife and daughter of the deceased.

Succinctly put, facts of case, as per claim petition, are that on the above said date and time, the deceased Sh. Ashok Kumar was riding his motorcycle bearing registration No. DL-9SAW-6111 on the correct side of the road.

When he reached near Pillar No. 135, Subroto Park, New Delhi, the offending vehicle bearing registration No.
09C088677N, which was being MACP No. 180/21 Page no.2 of 22 driven by respondent no. 1 in high speed and in rash and negligent manner, had hit the motorcycle of deceased from behind due to which he fell down on the road and came under the tyre of the offending vehicle.
It is further stated that the deceased was removed to Safdarjung Hospital, New Delhi where he was declared as 'brought dead' by the doctors.

3. Written statement has been filed on behalf of respondent wherein it is stated that the the alleged offending vehicle had never hit the motorcycle as there was no damage to the rear of the motorcycle.
It is further stated that the deceased tried to overtake from the left side of the vehicle inspite of the fact that there was very less space available for any motorcycle to overtake.
It is further stated that the speed of the offending vehicle was slow as there was no skid marks of the tyre on the road at the spot of accident.

4. It is pertinent to mention that the application under Order 1 Rule 10 CPC seeking impleadment of father of deceased namely Sh. Laxmi Narain was allowed vide order dated 12.01.2018 passed by the Ld. Predecessor of this Tribunal and the father of deceased was directed to be impleaded as respondent no. 3 in the present claim petition, however no written statement/reply has been filed on behalf of respondent no. 3.
Even he appeared on single date and thereafter stopped appearing.

5. On 10.03.2017, the following issues were framed by this tribunal:-
1.

Whether the deceased sustained fatal injuries in the accident which occurred on 12.07.2016 at about 06.50 pm, NH-8, Near Metro Pillar No. 135 caused by rash and negligent driving of vehicle No. 09C 086677N driven by MACP No. 180/21 Page no.3 of 22 respondent no. 1 and owned by respondent no. 2 ? The Tribunal has heard the arguments advanced by Sh. Sanjeev Kumar Malik, Ld. Counsel for petitioners and Sh. Sandeep Chandna, Ld. Counsel for respondent no. 1 and respondent no. 2/Union of India and has perused the entire record, including the case laws and written submissions filed on behalf of petitioners.

7. Now, the Tribunal proceeds to give findings on the issues framed in the succeeding paragraphs:
Whether the deceased sustained fatal injuries in the accident which occurred on 12.07.2016 at about 06.50 pm, NH-8, Near Metro Pillar No. 135 caused by rash and negligent driving of vehicle No. 09C 086677N driven by respondent no. 1 and owned by respondent no. 2 ? OPP.
Onus to prove this issue was upon the petitioners.
The first question that needs to be decided is whether the accident was caused by vehicle bearing registration No.09C086677.

In order to prove the same, the petitioners have examined on record the eye witness as per chargesheet Sh. Rohitashwa Dhanka as PW2 who deposed that he had not seen any accident involving an army truck or a motorcycle near Pillar No.
135, NH- 8, Dhaula Kaun.

Thereafter, the witness is confronted with his statement MACP No. 180/21 Page no.4 of 22 dated 12.07.2016 recorded by IO/SI Suresh Kumar as Ex. PW2/1, however, he denied having made any such statement to the police.
Hence, the prima eye witness has turned hostile in the present matter.

8. The petitioners thereafter examined on record Investigating Officer Retired SI Suresh Kumar as PW3 who deposed that on 12.07.2016 at about 7 pm, he had received a call regarding one accident and thereafter, he reached at the spot of accident along with Constable Rajesh Kumar.
He further deposed that he saw the army vehicle 2.5 ton bearing No. 09C086677N and one dead body was lying near the rear wheel of the said vehicle.
He further deposed that the motorcycle of deceased was also found there and he took photographs of spot from his mobile and sent the dead body to Safdarjung Hospital.
He further deposed that respondent no. 1 was found at the spot of accident and he took respondent no. 1 and the offending vehicle to the police chowki.
He further deposed that after registration of case, one Rohtash, S/o Sh. Bhagwan Singh visited the police chowki on the same day at around 9/9.30 pm and informed about the accident.
Thereafter, he recorded his statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C. as Ex. PW3/A and upon identification, he arrested respondent no. 1 in the present matter.
Thereafter, the DAR was filed before this tribunal after completion of investigation.
During cross examination, he admitted that he has not seen the accident himself.

9. Respondent no. 1 has examined himself as R1W1 who tendered his evidence by way of his affidavit Ex. R1W1/A wherein it is stated that on 12.07.2016, at around 07.05 pm, he was driving the alleged Sunita & Anr. vs . Vijay Kumar & Ors.

He was driving the said vehicle at the reasonable low speed in the left most lane of the road as he had to take a U turn and when they reached metro pillar no. 135 and 136, he heard noise from the rear of vehicle.
On which he applied brakes, stopped the vehicle and got down to see what had happened.
He saw a motorcyclist lying behind the left rear tyre and bleeding from his head.

He further stated that the deceased tried to overtake his vehicle from left side despite the fact that there was not sufficient space for overtaking and due to slippery on the road because of the rain in the afternoon, the motorcyclist slipped and came under the rear tyre of the vehicle.
During cross examination, he admitted that the FIR was lodged against him and the charge-sheet was also filed against him in the concerned court.
He admitted that he has not filed any complaint to any authority/court regarding his false implication in the criminal case.

10. Respondents no. 1 and 2 have also examined one Sh. Gurvinder Singh as R1W2 who tendered his evidence by way of affidavit Ex. R1W2/A, wherein he has stated that he was a co-driver of the alleged offending vehicle and has stated on the same lines of R1W1.

Despite his cross examination, nothing material came on record to discredit or disbelieve his testimony.
11.
During the course of final arguments, Ld. Counsel for petitioners has argued that the evidence of respondent no. 1 cannot be read in evidence as there is no pleadings on behalf of respondent no. 1.

In this regard, Ld. Counsel for petitioners has relied upon the judgment of the MACP No. 180/21 Page no.6 of 22 Hon'ble Delhi High Court in case Pankaj Tyagi & Anr. Vs. Rajender Kumar & Ors.,
2017 LawSuit(Del) 2732, decided on 21.07.2017, wherein it has been held as under :-
"3.

sentences.text: ....It may, however, be noted that appellants/defendant nos. 1 and 2 did not file the written statement as their right to file the written statement was closed and which order has become final.
Therefore, there is neither any pleading nor any evidence which could have been led or was led on behalf of the applicants/defendant nos.1 and 2 with respect to their pleas.

(ii) I also note that although the right of the appellants/defendant nos. 1 and 2 to file the written statement was closed, surprisingly they have been allowed to lead evidence, and which in law could not have been allowed because evidence is lead on a pleading.
Once there is no pleading then the defendant whose right has been closed to file the pleading, cannot lead any evidence.
At best, the entitlement of the defendant whose defence has been struck off is to cross examine the witnesses of the plaintiff.

12. The Tribunal has great regard for the law laid down by the superior court in the aforesaid judgment, however, the facts of the present matter are different as since beginning, there is one counsel appearing on behalf of respondents no. 1 and 2 and vide order dated 18.07.2017, Ld.

Further, invariably in numerous ordersheets, which are part of the record, the Ld. Counsel Sh. Manish Kumar has tendered his appearance for both the respondents, i.e. respondents no. 1 and 2 along with respondent MACP No.
180/21 Page no.7 of 22 no.1 in person.

Even vide order dated 30.01.2023, upon inquiry, the new counsel for both the aforesaid respondents Sh. Sandeep Chandna submitted that he is representing the respondents, as the offending vehicle belongs to Union of India.

Furthermore, the reply filed to the DAR is filed on behalf of respondent without specifically mentioning respondent no. 1 and 2 and the defence as deposed by witnesses R1W1 and R1W2 has been taken in the said reply.

Hence, it is clear that since beginning, i.e. from the time of filing of reply/pleadings, the same defence has been taken by the respondents no. 1 and 2 and the reply is filed on behalf of both the respondents, as already stated that R-1 was appearing in person with the said counsel.
Therefore, in view of the aforesaid discussions, it cannot be said that the respondent no. 1 has not filed his reply/written statement and that his evidence cannot be read.
Accordingly, it is held that the testimony of both the witnesses of respondent no. 1 is admissible in evidence and shall be read.
13. Now, coming back to the issue of rash and negligent driving by respondent no. 1 due to which the present accident is alleged to have occurred.
The eye witness produced by the petitioner, i.e. PW1 Sh. Rohitashwa Dhanka has turned totally hostile and stated that he has not seen the present accident.

However, PW3 Retired IO/SI Suresh Kumar has proved on record the investigation carried out by him and the charge-sheet was filed against respondent no. 1.
14.
On the point of sufficiency of chargesheet for proving rashness and negligence on behalf of driver of the offending vehicle, Ld.

Further, while he was taking left turn to the Unit Location, he heard the noise of accident and found the deceased lying under the left rear tyre of his vehicle.

16. The site plan has been perused carefully by the Tribunal along with the mechanical inspection report, which are part of the DAR and both points towards the fact that the deceased/motorcyclist was on the extreme left side of the offending vehicle and was driving on the verge of pavement and while R-1 tried to take left turn towards Unit Location, the motorcyclist got crushed under the rear wheel of the vehicle.

Hence, from the state of things as put on record, including the perusal of chargesheet (which is sufficient to prove rashness and negligence on the part of driver of the offending vehicle in view of the judgments relied upon by the petitioners), site plan, mechanical inspection report as well as testimony of witnesses, it stands proved on preponderance of probabilities that the aforesaid accident took place due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle bearing no. 09C-086677N and the said vehicle at that time was being driven by respondent no. 1 and owned by respondent no. 2 and that there was rashness/negligence on the part of the deceased as well.
Therefore, 50% amount out of the awarded amount be deducted towards the contributory negligence on the part of the deceased.
Hence, this issue is decided accordingly.

Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so, to what amount and from whom?
17.

As rashness and negligence on part of driver of the offending vehicle/respondent no. 1 has been proved, the petitioners have become entitled to compensation for death of their family member in the said MACP No. 180/21 Page no.10 of 22 accident, but the computation of compensation and liability to pay the same are required to be decided.
The compensation to which the petitioners are entitled shall be under the heads as discussed hereinafter.
(I) Loss of dependency 18.

The petitioner no. 1 Smt. Sunita, wife of deceased has stepped into the witness box as PW1 and filed her evidence by way of affidavit as Ex. PW-1/A wherein she has claimed that her deceased husband was doing the business of manufacturing and selling of belts, ties and school uniform at various shops and schools and was earning around Rs. 25,000/- per month.
During cross examination, he admitted that he has not filed any document showing the income of her deceased husband.

Since the employment and salary of the deceased has not been established on record, the minimum wages of unskilled person is taken into account as per rates prevalent in Delhi, which was Rs.
9,568/- per month at the time of accident, which is also mentioned in the written submissions filed on behalf of petitioners.
19. Further, PW1 has claimed in her affidavit that her deceased husband was aged about 32 years at the time of accident.
In order to prove the same, PW1 has tendered on record copy of Aadhar card and PAN card of her deceased husband as Ex. PW1/4 (OSR) and Ex. PW1/5 (OSR).
In both these documents, the date of birth of deceased was found recorded as 02.10.1984.
Going by these documents, the age of deceased at the time of accident i.e. on 12.07.2016 was about 31 years, 9 Sunita & Anr. vs . Vijay Kumar & Ors.
